discrepancy.note: Remsburg calls it a notable discrepancy that Mark bars remarriage after any divorce while Matthew allows it for fornication.

quotes.text: This is a notable discrepancy. According to Mark if a husband divorce his wife for any cause whatever he cannot lawfully marry another. According to Matthew if he divorce his wife for fornication he can lawfully marry again.
quotes.attr: John E. Remsburg (d. 1919), The Christ: A Critical Review and Analysis of the Evidences of His Existence (1909), on Mark 10:11.

sides.snippet: if she find no favor in his eyes, because he has found some unseemly thing in her, that he shall write her a bill of divorce
sides.verseText: When a man takes a wife, and marries her, then it shall be, if she find no favor in his eyes, because he has found some unseemly thing in her, that he shall write her a bill of divorce, and give it in her hand, and send her out of his house.

sides.snippet: Whoever divorces his wife, and marries another, commits adultery against her.
sides.verseText: He said to them, \"Whoever divorces his wife, and marries another, commits adultery against her.
